definition_zh: 戏服；服装；装束
definition_en: clothes worn for a play, a party or to look like someone
core_image: 万圣节南瓜斗篷一披，普通同学瞬间变成小巫师
scene: 学校艺术节要演小红帽，大家为戏服忙了一下午。 Her wolf costume made everyone laugh.
sceneCN: 这里 costume 是「戏服」（第 1 个义项：演出穿的服装）；句意是她的狼戏服把大家逗乐了。

derivatives.zh: 由 costume 加 -ed 构成，义为「穿着戏服的」
同根词 custom，义为「习俗」，是 costume 的词源核心

senses.title: Special clothes for a performance or party
senses.definition: clothes worn to look like a character in a play or at a party
senses.definitionCN: 为扮演角色或在聚会时穿的衣服
senses.example: The actors changed into their animal costumes backstage.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们在后台换上了动物戏服。
senses.why: Custom means habit, and stage clothes follow the custom of the character.
senses.whyCN: custom 意为习俗，戏服遵循角色的习俗。

senses.title: The traditional dress of a place or time
senses.definition: the typical clothes of a country, group or period
senses.definitionCN: 某国、某群体或某时代的典型服装
senses.example: She wore a beautiful national costume at the culture festival.
senses.exampleCN: 她在文化节上穿了漂亮的民族服装。
senses.why: Costume also means the dress a custom hands down through years.
senses.whyCN: costume 也指习俗流传多年的服饰。

senses.title: A set of clothes worn together
senses.definition: clothes of one style worn as a set
senses.definitionCN: 风格统一的一套衣服
senses.example: His swimming costume was left at home by mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他的泳衣被忘在了家里。
senses.why: The pieces belong together like one character's outfit.
senses.whyCN: 各件属于一套，如同一个角色的行头。

intro.en: Costume grew from the same root as custom, habits of dressing.
intro.cn: costume 与 custom 同根，都是穿着的习俗。

items.en: The Latin word consuetudo meant custom or habit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 consuetudo 意为习俗、习惯。

items.en: Italian costume meant custom, and then the customary style of dress.
items.cn: 意大利语 costume 意为习俗，进而指惯常的衣着风格。

items.en: French costume carried both custom and dress into learned writing.
items.cn: 法语 costume 兼指习俗与服饰，进入书面语。

items.en: English adopted costume in the eighteenth century for period dress.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪吸收 costume，指某时代的服装。

items.en: Theatre and parties made costume mean dress-up clothes today.
items.cn: 如今剧场与聚会让 costume 指化装服饰。

note.en: These words share the custom root or name clothes.
note.cn: 这些词共享 custom 词根或表示服装。

entries.definition: the place where officials check luggage

entries.definition: a set of clothes for one purpose

entries.definitionCN: 衣服（正式）

normal.en: costume parties need dress-up clothes.

abstract.cn: 想象万圣节的女巫帽和斗篷。

abstract.en: Picture a row of costumes on backstage hangers.
abstract.cn: 想象后台衣架上一排戏服。

abstract.en: Picture folk dancers in bright national dress.
abstract.cn: 想象穿鲜艳民族服装的民间舞者。

examples.cn: 我们为学校话剧做了恐龙戏服。

examples.en: Each region in China has its own traditional costume.

branches.cn: 传统服饰成套出现。

intro.en: The custom root dresses a whole family of words.
intro.cn: custom 词根装扮出一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin consuescere means to accustom.

definition_zh: 南方的；南部的；南方特有的
definition_en: in or from the south, or typical of the south
core_image: 地图上温暖的南部海岸线，阳光与棕榈树
scene: 这座南方城市冬天很温暖。 This southern city is warm in winter.
sceneCN: 这里 southern 是「南方的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座南方城市冬天很温暖。

derivatives.zh: 南方人
最南端的

senses.title: Of the south
senses.definition: located in or belonging to the south
senses.definitionCN: 位于或属于南方的
senses.example: This southern city is warm in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座南方城市冬天很温暖。
senses.why: This is the basic directional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的方位含义。

senses.title: Of a southern region
senses.definition: in the southern part of a particular country
senses.definitionCN: 位于某个国家南部的
senses.example: The southern border is guarded.
senses.exampleCN: 南部边界有人守卫。
senses.why: A region gives the direction a local name.
senses.whyCN: 地区给方向一个本地的名字。

senses.title: Typical of the south
senses.definition: characteristic of the south, such as its weather or speech
senses.definitionCN: 具有南方特征的，如气候或口音
senses.example: She speaks with a southern accent.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话带南方口音。
senses.why: Place shapes manner, and the adjective records it.
senses.whyCN: 地方塑造风格，形容词记录了这种风格。

intro.en: Southern is south with an old adjective ending.
intro.cn: southern 是 south 加一个古老的形容词词尾。

items.en: Sutherne meant of the south.
items.cn: sutherne 意为南方的。

items.en: The form became southerne.
items.cn: 词形变为 southerne。

items.en: Southern named regions and their weather.
items.cn: southern 指地区及其气候。

items.en: It also named accents and customs.
items.cn: 它也指口音与习俗。

items.en: Southern Hemisphere fixed it in geography.
items.cn: Southern Hemisphere 把它固定在地理用语中。

note.en: Southern is compared with the other compass adjectives.
note.cn: 把 southern 与其他方位形容词作比较。

entries.definition: of the east

entries.definition: going toward the south

entries.definition: of the hot regions near the equator
entries.definitionCN: 热带的

normalIntro.en: Southern puts the south in front of a noun.
normalIntro.cn: southern 把「南方」放在名词前面。

normal.cn: 这座南方城市冬天很温暖。

normal.en: The southern border is guarded.

normal.en: She speaks with a southern accent.

normal.en: The southern coast is full of small bays.

abstract.en: Southern is a direction wearing local clothes.
abstract.cn: southern 是穿上地方衣裳的方向。

abstract.en: The south is warm in weather and in memory.
abstract.cn: 南方在天气里温暖，在记忆里也温暖。

abstract.en: Every region makes its own version of the same word.

examples.en: She speaks with a southern accent.

dict_mnemonic.text: southern 由 south 加 -ern 构成，类似 northern、eastern、western；southern part 是「南部」，Southern Hemisphere 是「南半球」，southern accent 是「南方口音」。

root: 来自古英语 sutherne（南方的），由 south 加形容词词尾构成，核心义为方位上的南方及其地方特征。

sensesIntro.en: Southern means of the south, of a southern region, or typical of the south.
sensesIntro.cn: southern 意为南方的、南部地区的，或具有南方特征的。

core.cn: 附着在地方或事物上的「南方」。

branches.en: A warm city sits low on the map.

definition_zh: 胸；胸腔；箱子；柜子
definition_en: the upper front part of the body between the neck and the stomach; a large strong box with a lid for storing things
core_image: 厚木箱扣着大铁锁，或胸膛起伏的一次深呼吸
scene: 体育课跑完四百米，同学们手按胸口大口喘气。 After the 400-metre run, we all held our chests and panted.
sceneCN: 这里 chest 是「胸」（第 1 个义项：颈到胃之间的身体前部）；句意为跑完四百米后大家手按胸口喘气。

derivatives.zh: 由 chest 加 -y 构成，义为「胸部不适的；（咳嗽）带痰音的」
由 chest（古义）加 nut 构成，义为「栗子；栗树」

senses.title: The upper front part of the body
senses.definition: the front upper part of the body between the neck and the stomach
senses.definitionCN: 颈部与胃部之间的身体前上部
senses.example: After the 400-metre run, we all held our chests and panted.
senses.exampleCN: 跑完四百米后，大家都手按胸口喘气。
senses.why: The body's front box that holds the heart and lungs was named after the box that holds treasures.
senses.whyCN: 盛着心与肺的身体前箱，因盛放珍宝的箱子而得名。

senses.title: A large strong box with a lid
senses.definition: a large, strong box with a lid, used for storing or carrying things
senses.definitionCN: 带盖的大型坚固箱子，用于储存或搬运
senses.example: The old wooden chest in the attic holds winter clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 阁楼上的旧木箱装着过冬衣物。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the container itself: a strong box that keeps things safe inside.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是容器本身：一只把物品妥善收藏的坚固木箱。

senses.title: A set of drawers for storing clothes
senses.definition: a piece of furniture with drawers for storing clothes
senses.definitionCN: 带抽屉用于存放衣物的家具
senses.example: She folded the shirts into the chest of drawers.
senses.exampleCN: 她把衬衫叠好放进五斗柜。
senses.why: The storing box grew furniture-like, divided into drawers that still 'keep' things.
senses.whyCN: 储物之箱逐渐家具化，分成一只只仍司「收纳」之职的抽屉。

senses.title: The box-like middle of the body in speech
senses.definition: the chest as the seat of feelings or strength
senses.definitionCN: 作为情感或力量所在的胸膛
senses.example: He beat his chest after winning the race.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得比赛后他捶胸欢呼。
senses.why: Because the chest visibly rises with strong feeling, it stands for feeling itself.
senses.whyCN: 胸膛随强烈情绪明显起伏，便被借代为情感本身。

intro.en: Chest began as a word for a strong box, and the body part borrowed the container's name.
intro.cn: chest 起初指坚固的箱子，身体部位借用了这个容器的名字。

items.en: Old English cest meant a box or basket for storing things.
items.cn: 古英语 cest 指储物的箱子或篮子。

items.en: It goes back to Latin cista, a woven box or basket.
items.cn: 其源头是拉丁语 cista，指编织的箱篮。

items.en: Latin cista came from Greek kiste, a woven chest.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cista 又源自希腊语 kiste（编织箱）。

items.en: Middle English chest named the box and, by likeness, the rib cage.
items.cn: 中古英语 chest 既指箱子，又因形似转指胸廓。

items.en: Modern English chest covers the body part, the box and the drawer furniture.
items.cn: 现代英语的 chest 兼指身体部位、箱柜与抽屉家具。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects containers and body words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收纳物与身体类词。

definition_zh: 注意到；察觉；通知；告知；告示；通告；短评
definition_en: to become aware of something; also a formal statement that tells people something, a written public sign, and a short review in a newspaper
core_image: 眼睛忽然停在某处细小的地方，心里咯噔一下：我看见了
scene: 雨后的公交站牌下，等车的人无意间抬头，视线落在路对面那件深色外套上。 She noticed a small stain on the man's collar as he stood in line.
sceneCN: 这里 notice 是「注意到、察觉」（第 1 个义项：用眼睛或心思捕捉到某个细节）；句意为排队时她注意到前面那人衣领上有一小块污渍。图中可辨识物件：候车的人、路牌、雨后的地面。

collocations.zh: 在很短的通知时间内；临时

derivatives.zh: 由动词 notice 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「容易被注意到的；明显的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 noticed 构成，义为「未被注意到的」
由 noticeable 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」

senses.title: To become aware of something
senses.definition: to see, hear or realize something, often without deliberately looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 看见、听见或意识到某事，往往并非刻意寻找
senses.example: She noticed a small stain on his collar.
senses.exampleCN: 她注意到他衣领上有一小块污渍。
senses.why: The Latin source notitia names the state of something being known, so this verb starts from a fact entering your mind rather than from a deliberate search.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notitia 指「被知道的状态」，所以这个动词的起点是某个事实自己进了心里，而不是刻意去找。

senses.title: A formal statement that tells someone something
senses.definition: an official or formal message or warning given to a person who must act on it
senses.definitionCN: 正式或官方地告知某人的消息、警告，收信人往往要据此行动
senses.example: The tenant received notice that the rent would rise in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 租客收到了房租将在春天上涨的通知。
senses.why: Once notitia means a piece of knowledge, it can also mean handing that knowledge to someone who must respond, which is why the noun turns official.
senses.whyCN: notitia 既然能指「一条已知的消息」，也就能指把这条消息交给需要作出回应的人，于是这个名词带上了正式、官方的色彩。

senses.title: A written sign giving public information
senses.definition: a piece of paper or a sign placed in a public spot to tell people something
senses.definitionCN: 张贴在公共场所、用来告知信息的纸片或牌子
senses.example: A notice on the door said the library would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 门上的一张告示说图书馆会提前关门。
senses.why: A written notice is knowledge fixed on paper, so the same word moves from what is told to what is posted for everyone to read.
senses.whyCN: 书面告示就是把「已知的消息」固定在纸上，同一个词便从「被告知的事」转到「贴出来给所有人看的东西」。

senses.title: A short review of a performance or book
senses.definition: a short newspaper article that judges a play, film or book
senses.definitionCN: 报刊上评价戏剧、电影或书籍的短文
senses.example: The young actor got a favourable notice in the morning paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻演员在晨报上得到了一篇好评。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century papers printed such reviews beside announcements, so a word for an announcement came to name a printed judgement of a performance as well.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的报纸把剧评和各类公告排在一起，于是原本表示「通告」的词也用来指印在报上的演出评价。

intro.en: Notice comes from a Latin noun for being known, travelled through French, and keeps both the act of seeing and the official statement in modern English.
intro.cn: notice 源自拉丁语中表示「被知晓」的名词，经法语传入英语，至今同时保留「看见」与「正式告知」两条线索。

items.en: The verb noscere meant to get to know or to recognise, and it is the root behind a whole family of words about knowledge.
items.cn: 动词 noscere 意为认识、认出，是整族「知识」词汇共同的根。

items.en: Notitia named the state of being known, and could also mean a piece of information or an acquaintance.
items.cn: notitia 指「被知道的状态」，也可指一则消息或一位相识的人。

items.en: Old French kept notice for information, knowledge and a warning, and passed the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语保留 notice 一词，表示消息、知识与警告，并在诺曼时期之后把它传入英语。

items.en: In Middle English the word covered both what a person came to know and the formal warning that told people what to do.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，这个词既指一个人得知的事，也指告诉人们该怎么做的正式警告。

items.en: Modern English adds the public written sign and the newspaper review, while the verb stays close to simply seeing something.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上公共场所的书面告示与报刊短评，而动词仍旧贴近「看见了什么」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin root for knowing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for perceiving.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「知道」词根上的词；近义组收表示察觉的动词。

entries.definition: An idea or belief held in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 头脑中持有的一种想法或看法。

entries.definition: Important or unusual enough to deserve attention.
entries.definitionCN: 重要或不寻常到值得留意的。

entries.definition: A system of written signs used in music or mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐或数学中使用的一套书写符号。

entries.definition: The state of being widely known for something bad.
entries.definitionCN: 因坏事而广为人知的状态。

entries.definition: To become aware of something through the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 通过感官察觉到某事物。

entries.definition: To watch something carefully and take in the details.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细观察并留意细节。

entries.definition: To find something that is hidden or easy to miss.
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏或容易漏掉的事物。

entries.definition: To make out something that is not obvious.
entries.definitionCN: 辨认出并不明显的事物。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin root for knowing, and its two halves, seeing and telling, both grow from the same idea of something becoming known.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词长在表示「知道」的拉丁词根上，它的两半——看见与告知——都出自「某事被知道」这同一个念头。

normal.en: Noscere in Latin means to get to know, so notice is what happens when something becomes known to your eyes.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 noscere 意为认识，所以 notice 就是某样东西被你的眼睛知道的那一刻。

normal.en: Notice entered English first as a noun from notitia; the verb came later by using the noun as an action.
normal.cn: notice 先以名词身份从 notitia 进入英语，动词是后来把这个名词当动作来用。

normal.en: Noticeable adds -able to notice, meaning able to be noticed, and the final e stays before the suffix.
normal.cn: noticeable 在 notice 后加 -able，意为「能被注意到的」，词尾的 e 在加后缀时保留。

normal.en: Notify is built differently: notus plus -ify, to make known, so it means telling someone officially rather than merely seeing.
normal.cn: notify 的构造不同：notus 加 -ify，意为「使被知道」，所以它指正式告知某人，而不只是看见。

normal.en: At short notice means with very little warning, because notice here is the time given before something happens.
normal.cn: at short notice 意为几乎没有提前告知，因为这里的 notice 指事情发生前留给你的那段时间。

abstract.en: A notice board holds many small facts pinned in place, each waiting for the one person who needs it.
abstract.cn: 布告栏上钉着许多小事，每一件都在等那个恰好需要它的人。

abstract.en: Seeing and telling are two ends of one thread: what you notice may later have to be announced to others.
abstract.cn: 看见与告知是同一条线的两端：你注意到的事，后来可能要告知别人。

abstract.en: A word that can mean a glance and a resignation letter shows how much weight lies in simply being told.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能指一瞥，又能指辞职信，说明「被告知」这件事本身有多重。

examples.en: She noticed a small stain on his collar.
examples.cn: 她注意到他衣领上有一小块污渍。

examples.en: The staff were given notice of the change in the rota.
examples.cn: 员工们收到了排班变更的通知。

examples.en: A handwritten notice was pinned beside the lift.
examples.cn: 电梯旁钉着一张手写的告示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺替事」——答应替人办事，就得时时留意、件件告知；notice 既是留意，也是通知。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 notitia（被知道的状态），源于 noscere（认识），经古法语 notice 进入英语；同族词多与「知道、记号」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something entering your awareness; from there the word splits into the private act of seeing and the public act of telling, with the posted sign and the printed review as its outward forms.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是某样东西进入你的意识；由此分出私下「看见」与公开「告知」两条路，张贴的告示与报刊短评则是它外在的形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of eyes stopping on one small detail while the mind registers it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双眼睛停在某个细小之处，心里记下了它。

branches.en: a glance that catches a stain on a collar
branches.cn: 一眼瞥见衣领上的污渍

branches.en: a fact moving from one mind to another
branches.cn: 一件事从一个人心里传到另一个人心里

branches.en: a sheet of paper pinned beside a door
branches.cn: 钉在门边的一张纸

branches.en: a letter that warns of a coming change
branches.cn: 预告即将变动的一封信

branches.en: a short column judging a new play
branches.cn: 评价一部新戏的短栏

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for knowing and a Latin noun for being known, then passes through French without carrying an English prefix of its own.
intro.cn: 这个词立在表示「认识」的拉丁动词与表示「被知道」的拉丁名词上，经法语进入英语，本身不带英语前缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to get to know, to recognise

derivatives.zh: 同一词根上的名词，义为「概念；想法」
同一词根上的形容词，义为「值得注意的」

definition_zh: 平衡；余额；天平；剩余部分；使平衡；权衡
definition_en: an even state in which nothing falls or is heavier, or the money left in an account
core_image: 一架天平两端各放一枚砝码，横梁停在水平
scene: 窄墙上，她张开双臂，慢慢把身体稳住。 She held out her arms to keep her balance on the narrow wall.
sceneCN: 这里 balance 是「平衡」（第 1 个义项：身体不倾倒的均衡状态）；句意为她张开双臂，在窄墙上保持平衡。

pos.zh: 名词：平衡；余额；天平；剩余部分

derivatives.zh: 由 balance 加 -ed 构成，义为「均衡的、平稳的」
由否定前缀 im- 与 balance 构成，义为「失衡」
由否定前缀 un- 与 balanced 构成，义为「不平衡的；失常的」
由 counter-「对抗」与 balance 构成，义为「抗衡物、平衡力」

senses.title: An even state
senses.definition: a steady state in which weight or force is even and nothing falls
senses.definitionCN: 重量或力量均匀、不会倒下的稳定状态
senses.example: She held out her arms to keep her balance.
senses.exampleCN: 她张开双臂保持平衡。
senses.why: The Latin word named a pair of scales with two equal pans, so the first sense is the even state of the beam.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本指两盘相等的一架天平，所以第一个义项就是横梁持平的均衡状态。

senses.title: Money left in an account
senses.definition: the amount of money remaining in a bank account after payments
senses.definitionCN: 银行账户在支付之后剩余的金额
senses.example: He checked his bank balance before buying the ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 买票之前他查了账户余额。
senses.why: Money in and money out are weighed like two pans; what is left when they even out is the balance.
senses.whyCN: 进账与出账像两只秤盘一样被称量，两者相抵后剩下的就是 balance。

senses.title: A weighing device
senses.definition: a device with two pans for weighing things by comparing weights
senses.definitionCN: 有两个秤盘、通过比较重量来称物的器具
senses.example: The old balance stood on the shop counter.
senses.exampleCN: 那架旧天平摆在商店柜台上。
senses.why: This is the original object itself: the instrument whose two pans must come level.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的那件器物本身：两只秤盘必须保持水平的天平。

senses.title: The rest of something
senses.definition: the part of something that remains after the other parts are used
senses.definitionCN: 其他部分用掉之后剩下的那部分
senses.example: The balance of the money went to the school.
senses.exampleCN: 剩下的钱给了学校。
senses.why: Once one side of an account is settled, what is left over is what keeps the two sides level, so the remainder is also the balance.
senses.whyCN: 账目的一边结清后，剩下用来让两边持平的部分就是余额，于是「剩余部分」也叫 balance。

senses.title: To keep steady
senses.definition: to keep something in a steady position so that it does not fall
senses.definitionCN: 使某物保持稳定位置而不倒下
senses.example: He balanced the box on one hand.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一只手把箱子端平。
senses.why: The verb turns the even state into an action: holding the object so that the two sides stay level.
senses.whyCN: 动词把均衡状态变成动作：扶住物体，让两边保持水平。

senses.title: To weigh two things against each other
senses.definition: to compare two needs or choices and give each a fair share of attention
senses.definitionCN: 比较两种需要或选择，并各给适当的重视
senses.example: She balanced study and sport every week.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周都兼顾学习与运动。
senses.why: When the two pans hold different things, the mind weighs them; giving each its fair weight is the abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 当两只秤盘装着不同的东西时，人会在心里称量；给每一方适当的重量，就是抽象的「权衡」。

intro.en: Balance goes back to a Latin name for a two-pan scale and reached English through French.
intro.cn: balance 可追溯到拉丁语中「双盘天平」的名称，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Lanx was the Latin word for a flat dish or the pan of a scale; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: lanx 是拉丁语「浅盘、秤盘」，更早来源不确定。

items.en: The prefix bi- meaning two plus lanx formed bilanx, describing a scale with two pans.
items.cn: 表示「二」的前缀 bi- 加 lanx 构成 bilanx，指有两隻秤盘的天平。

items.en: Old French balance carried both the instrument and the idea of an even state into English.
items.cn: 古法语 balance 把「天平」这件器具与「均衡」的观念一起带入英语。

items.en: Middle English used the word for scales and for the even state of anything weighed.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指天平，也指被称量之物的均衡状态。

items.en: The financial sense of the money left in an account develops from the image of two sides that must come level.
items.cn: 账户余额这一财务义项，是从「两边必须持平」的意象发展出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on balance or sharing its Latin pieces; the near-meaning group gathers words for steadiness, weighing, and what is left over.
note.cn: 形近组收由 balance 构成或共享拉丁构件的词；近义组收表示稳定、称量与剩余的词。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning steady, even, or giving fair weight to each side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「均衡的、平稳的」，由 balance 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: A state in which one side is heavier or stronger than the other.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失衡」，指一方比另一方更重或更强。

entries.definition: A weight or force that balances another one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抗衡物、平衡力」，指抵消另一方重量的东西。

entries.definition: A small platform outside a window; it only looks similar and comes from a different Italian word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「阳台」；只是拼写与发音相近，词源不同，来自意大利语而非天平。

entries.definition: A state of perfect balance between opposing forces; more technical than balance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「平衡、均衡」，指对立力量之间的完美均势，比 balance 更专业。

entries.definition: The quality of being firm and not shaking; it stresses the result rather than the weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「稳定、平稳」，强调不晃动的结果，而不含称量的意味。

entries.definition: The part that is left over; it matches the fourth sense without the scale image.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剩余部分」，对应第四个义项，但不带天平的意象。

entries.definition: A device for weighing; the everyday word for the third sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「秤、天平」，是第三个义项的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin pieces bi- and lanx, the suffix -ance, and the everyday phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁构件 bi- 与 lanx、后缀 -ance，以及这个词实际出现的日常搭配。

normal.en: Bilanx means two pans: bi- is two, lanx is a pan, and a balance is the beam that keeps them level.
normal.cn: bilanx 意为「两只秤盘」：bi- 是二，lanx 是盘，balance 就是让两盘持平的横梁。

normal.en: The noun suffix -ance names a state, so balance is the state of being level.
normal.cn: 名词后缀 -ance 表示状态，所以 balance 就是「处于水平」的状态。

normal.en: Keep your balance and lose your balance are the two daily phrases about the body.
normal.cn: keep your balance 与 lose your balance 是日常谈身体平衡的两个固定说法。

normal.en: A bank balance is the money that keeps the two sides of an account level.
normal.cn: bank balance 就是让账户两边持平的那笔钱。

normal.en: Balance the budget means making income and spending weigh the same.
normal.cn: balance the budget 意为让收入与支出称起来一样重。

abstract.en: Picture a beam with one coin on each pan: the moment it stops moving is the moment the word describes.
abstract.cn: 想象横梁两端各放一枚硬币：它停止晃动的那一刻，正是这个词描述的状态。

abstract.en: The same beam can hold money instead of coins, and then the balance is what is left in the account.
abstract.cn: 同一根横梁上也可以放钱而不是硬币，这时 balance 就是账户里剩下的数目。

abstract.en: When two duties sit on the pans, keeping the beam level is not a physical act but a choice.
abstract.cn: 当两只秤盘上放着两份责任时，让横梁保持水平不再是体力动作，而是一种选择。

examples.en: She held out her arms to keep her balance on the narrow wall.
examples.cn: 她张开双臂，在窄墙上保持平衡。

examples.en: He checked his bank balance before buying the ticket.
examples.cn: 买票之前他查了账户余额。

examples.en: A good student balances study and rest.
examples.cn: 好学生懂得兼顾学习与休息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「白兰丝」——白兰丝挂在秤两端，刚好一样重：平衡

root: 拉丁语 bilanx「双盘天平」由 bi-「二」+ lanx「秤盘、浅盘」构成，lanx 更早来源不确定；经古法语 balance 进入英语。由「天平持平」引申出「余额、剩余部分、权衡」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of balance all come from one beam with two pans: the even state, the money that keeps an account level, the instrument itself, what is left over, the act of holding something steady, and the mental act of weighing two needs.
sensesIntro.cn: balance 的六个义项都来自一根架着两盘的横梁：均衡状态、让账户持平的余额、天平本身、剩余部分、扶稳物体的动作，以及心里权衡两种需要。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam with a pan on each side stops moving and rests exactly level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根两端各挂一只秤盘的横梁停止晃动，正好停在水平位置。

branches.en: THE STATE: two equal weights leave the beam level, and that even state is the first sense.
branches.cn: 状态线：两份相等的重量让横梁持平，这个均衡状态就是第一义。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: money in and money out are weighed, and what keeps the two sides level is the balance.
branches.cn: 账目线：进账与出账被称量，让两边持平的那部分就是余额。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: before it was an idea, balance was the physical scale on the counter.
branches.cn: 器物线：在成为观念之前，balance 就是柜台上那架实体天平。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the verb holds an object so that it does not tip.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词指扶住物体，使它不倾倒。

branches.en: THE MIND: two duties sit on the pans, and balancing them becomes a fair judgment.
branches.cn: 心智线：两份责任放在秤盘上，让它们平衡就成了一种公正的判断。

intro.en: Balance is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin noun, then enlarged by English suffixes and a combining prefix.
intro.cn: balance 由拉丁语前缀与拉丁名词构成，再由英语后缀和组合前缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin lanx and bilanx are recorded, so only the deeper origin of lanx is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lanx 与 bilanx 均有文献记录，只有 lanx 更早的来源不确定。

items.exampleCN: 它在 bilanx 中给出「两只秤盘」的意思。

items.example: It is the direct source of the word.

items.example: It forms balance from the French stem.

definition_zh: 两者都不；也不；既不……也不
definition_en: not one and not the other of two things; also used before nor in a paired construction, and as an adverb meaning also not
core_image: 桌上并排放着两只杯子，两只都被推回原处，没有一只被端起
scene: 桌上并排放着两杯饮料，孩子看了看，把它们一起推回桌子中央。 Neither of the two cups had been touched.
sceneCN: 这里 neither 是「两者都不」（第 1 个义项：两个当中一个也不是）；句意为两只杯子都没有被动过。图中可辨识物件：两只杯子、干净的桌面。

derivatives.zh: 与 neither 共用古英语 hwæþer（两者中的哪一个）这一词干，义为「两者中的任一个」，是同源词而非严格派生词
同出古英语 hwæþer，义为「是否」，与 neither 共享表示「两者中哪一个」的词干

senses.title: Not one and not the other of two
senses.definition: not either of two people or things that have just been mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚提到的两个人或两样东西，一个也不是
senses.example: Neither of the two answers is correct.
senses.exampleCN: 两个答案都不对。
senses.why: The word is a contraction of the Old English phrase for not which of the two, so its whole job is to sweep both options away in a single gesture.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是古英语中「两者中的哪一个都不是」这一说法的缩合，所以它全部的活儿就是用一次动作把两个选项一起扫掉。

senses.title: Paired with nor to deny both
senses.definition: used with nor to connect two things that are both denied
senses.definitionCN: 与 nor 连用，连接两样都被否定的事物
senses.example: Neither the driver nor the passengers were hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 司机和乘客都没有受伤。
senses.why: Since the first half already denies both members of a pair, English repeats the denial with nor so that each item is explicitly ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 词的前半已经把一对中的两个都否定了，英语再用 nor 重复一次否定，让每一项都被明确排除。

senses.title: Also not, in agreement with a negative
senses.definition: used after a negative statement to say that the same is true of another person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定句之后，表示另一个人或事物情况相同
senses.example: I cannot swim, and neither can my brother.
senses.exampleCN: 我不会游泳，我弟弟也不会。
senses.why: The denying force of the pronoun is reused as a short adverb, so a whole negative clause is compressed into one word plus a reversed subject and verb.
senses.whyCN: 代词里的否定力量被挪作简短副词，于是一整个否定从句被压缩成一个词加倒装的主语和动词。

intro.en: Neither is an Old English contraction of a phrase meaning not either, built from a negative word and the word for which of two.
intro.cn: neither 是古英语里「不是两者中的任何一个」这一说法的缩合，由一个否定词和表示「两者中哪一个」的词合成。

items.en: Na was the plain negative word, meaning no or not, and it supplied the first half of the compound.
items.cn: nā 是普通的否定词，意为「不、没有」，构成复合词的前半。

items.en: Hwaether meant which of the two, and it is the same word that became whether in modern English.
items.cn: hwæþer 意为「两者中的哪一个」，就是现代英语 whether 的来源。

items.en: Nahwther meant not either of the two, and in speech it was shortened to forms such as neither.
items.cn: nāhwæþer 意为「两者中哪一个都不是」，在口语中缩短成 neither 这类形式。

items.en: Middle English settled on spellings like neither, and the word worked both as a pronoun and as a conjunction.
items.cn: 中古英语固定为 neither 这类写法，这个词同时作代词和连词。

items.en: Modern English keeps it as the pronoun, in the paired construction with nor, and in the adverb use of short negative replies.
items.cn: 现代英语保留它作代词、作与 nor 搭配的配对结构，以及简短否定回答里的副词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the old element for which of two or merely the spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words of outright denial.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「两者中哪一个」这一古老成分的词，以及只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示彻底否定的词。

entries.definition: One or the other of two, the positive partner of this pair of words.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中的任意一个，是这对词里的肯定一方。

entries.definition: Lower or underneath, as in the old phrase the nether world; it only looks like neither, and the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 下面的、下方的，如旧说法「下界」；只是与 neither 拼写相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: Neither masculine nor feminine in grammar; the Latin word means neither, but it is not the English source.
entries.definitionCN: 语法上既非阳性也非阴性；拉丁语原词意为「两者都不」，但它不是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: Not one of any number, used for more than two as well as for two.
entries.definitionCN: 任何数量中一个也没有，既可用于两个，也可用于更多。

entries.definition: And not, used to continue a negative statement.
entries.definitionCN: 也不，用于延续一个否定说法。

entries.definition: No person at all, used of people rather than of things.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人也没有，用于人而不用于物。

normalIntro.en: The word is a contraction of not plus which of two, and that double denial is what every one of its uses carries.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「不」加上「两者中哪一个」的缩合，它每一种用法都带着这层双重否定。

normal.en: The first half is an old negative word, so neither always denies before it chooses.
normal.cn: 前半是一个古老的否定词，所以 neither 总是先否定，再谈选择。

normal.en: The second half is the same element that gives English whether, so the word is literally not whether of the two.
normal.cn: 后半就是给英语 whether 的那个成分，所以这个词字面是「两者中的哪一个都不」。

normal.en: Neither is followed by a singular verb in careful writing, because it denies each member separately.
normal.cn: 在严谨的写作里 neither 后接单数动词，因为它对每一个成员分别加以否定。

normal.en: The paired pattern needs nor, not or, since the second item is denied as well.
normal.cn: 配对结构要用 nor 而不是 or，因为第二项同样被否定。

normal.en: In short replies the word brings inversion, as in neither do I, which copies the order of a question.
normal.cn: 在简短回答里它会带来倒装，如 neither do I，照搬了疑问句的词序。

abstract.en: A word made of not plus which of two shows that a choice can be refused before it is even offered.
abstract.cn: 一个由「不」加「两者中哪一个」构成的词说明：选择可以在被提出之前就被拒绝。

abstract.en: Neither is the grammar of a closed door: two ways stand open, and both are declared shut.
abstract.cn: neither 是一扇关上的门的语法：两条路摆在面前，两条都被宣布关闭。

abstract.en: Its three jobs as pronoun, conjunction and adverb show how one small denial can hold a whole clause together.
abstract.cn: 它兼作代词、连词和副词，说明一个小小的否定能撑起整个从句。

examples.en: Neither of the two cups had been touched.
examples.cn: 两只杯子都没有被动过。

examples.en: Neither the driver nor the passengers were hurt.
examples.cn: 司机和乘客都没有受伤。

examples.en: I cannot swim, and neither can my brother.
examples.cn: 我不会游泳，我弟弟也不会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「你惹」——两个都惹了你，于是一个也不选；记住 neither 是两者都不。

root: 古英语 nā（不）加 hwæþer（两者中的哪一个）缩合为 nāhwæþer，后简作 neither；与 either、whether 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the denial of both members of a pair; it divides into the pronoun, the paired conjunction with nor and the adverb of agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把一对中的两个一起否定；由此分出代词、与 nor 搭配的连词，以及表示「也不」的副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two cups standing side by side, both pushed back untouched.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只杯子并排放着，两只都被推回原处，谁也没被端起。

branches.cn: 两只杯子被一起推回桌子中央

branches.en: two doors closed at the same moment
branches.cn: 两扇门在同一刻被关上

branches.en: a sign listing two rules, both crossed out
branches.cn: 一块列着两条规定的牌子，两条都被划掉

branches.en: two names missing from a list of guests
branches.cn: 宾客名单上缺了两个名字

branches.en: one person shaking his head, then another
branches.cn: 一个人摇头，另一个人也跟着摇头

intro.en: The word is a contraction of two Old English pieces, a negative word and the element for which of two, and those pieces still explain its grammar.
intro.cn: 这个词是两块古英语构件的缩合：一个否定词，一个表示「两者中哪一个」的成分；这两块构件至今解释着它的语法。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no reliable Latin cognate; its two parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词；它的两个构件都来自古英语。

definition_zh: 脆的；酥脆的；清爽的； crisp 的动词义为使发脆
definition_en: firm and dry so it makes a clean breaking sound; fresh and pleasantly cold
core_image: 咬下去咔嚓一声的清爽脆响
scene: 秋游野餐时，打开一包新买的薯片，咔嚓声让全组同学都笑了。 The chips stay crisp inside the sealed bag.
sceneCN: 这里 crisp 是「脆的」（第 1 个义项：咬起来干脆有声）；句意是薯片在密封袋里保持酥脆。

derivatives.zh: 由 crisp 加副词后缀构成，义为「干脆利落地」
由 crisp 加名词后缀构成，义为「酥脆；清爽」
同义变体，义为「酥脆的」

senses.title: Firm and making a clean break
senses.definition: hard, dry and fresh so it breaks with a pleasant sound
senses.definitionCN: 又硬又干又新鲜，咬断时发出悦耳的脆响
senses.example: The winter apples are crisp and sweet.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天的苹果脆甜可口。
senses.why: The core image is a clean snap when you bite, so dry firmness that snaps is crisp.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是咬下时干脆的一声断响，所以能咔嚓一声断开的干硬就是 crisp。

senses.title: Fresh and pleasantly cold
senses.definition: air or weather that is cold, dry and refreshing
senses.definitionCN: 凉爽干燥、令人神清气爽的空气或天气
senses.example: We enjoyed the crisp air on the morning walk.
senses.exampleCN: 晨走时我们享受着清爽的空气。
senses.why: A clean snap in the mouth feels sharp and fresh; the same freshness rides on cold air.
senses.whyCN: 口中的干脆感是清冽新鲜的；同样的新鲜感也附着在冷空气中。

senses.title: Short, clear and quick
senses.definition: said or done in a quick, clear way without extra words
senses.definitionCN: 说话或做事干脆利落，没有多余的话
senses.example: The coach gave a crisp answer to every question.
senses.exampleCN: 教练对每个问题都给出了干脆的回答。
senses.why: A snap has no wobble, so speech without extra words is also crisp.
senses.whyCN: 脆响没有一点拖泥带水，所以没有废话的话语也是 crisp。

senses.title: To make or become firm and dry
senses.definition: to make food firm and dry by cooking, or to turn that way
senses.definitionCN: 通过烹饪使食物变干变脆，或指食物变脆的过程
senses.example: The bacon crisps nicely in the hot pan.
senses.exampleCN: 培根在热锅里煎得香脆。
senses.why: Cooking drives water out, leaving the snap behind, so the verb simply means to create the snap.
senses.whyCN: 烹饪把水分赶走，留下脆响，所以动词义就是制造脆响。

intro.en: Crisp traces back to Latin words about curly hair and stiffened surfaces.
intro.cn: crisp 可追溯到拉丁语中与卷发、挺硬表面相关的词。

items.en: The Latin crispus meant curly or stiff with tiny waves.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crispus 意为卷曲的、带细小波纹而硬挺的。

items.en: Old French kept cresp, meaning curly, and applied it to surfaces.
items.cn: 古法语保留 cresp，意为卷曲的，并用于描述表面。

items.en: English borrowed crisp in Old English times via Germanic contact, first about curly hair.
items.cn: 英语经由日耳曼接触在古英语时期借入 crisp，起初形容卷发。

items.en: The sense moved from curls to dry firm surfaces that snap.
items.cn: 词义从「卷曲」转向干燥挺硬、一折就断的表面。

items.en: Today crisp describes food, air, writing and even banknotes.
items.cn: 如今 crisp 形容食物、空气、文风甚至钞票。

note.en: These words share the crisp family or name snap and freshness.
note.cn: 这些词属于 crisp 词族，或表示脆响与清新。

entries.definitionCN: 酥脆的

entries.definition: in a crisp manner
entries.definitionCN: 干脆利落地

entries.definition: the quality of being crisp

entries.definition: in Britain, a thin potato snack
entries.definitionCN: 薯片（英式叫法）

entries.definition: making a loud breaking sound
entries.definitionCN: 嘎吱脆的

entries.definition: hard but easily broken
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的

entries.definition: newly picked or made
entries.definitionCN: 新鲜的

entries.definition: quick, active and cool
entries.definitionCN: 利落的；凉爽的

entries.definition: a quick clean break
entries.definitionCN: 脆响；折断

normalIntro.en: Sound and surface images fix crisp quickly.
normalIntro.cn: 声音与表面的意象能快速锁定 crisp。

normal.en: crisp sounds like its own snap: kr-i-sp.
normal.cn: crisp 的发音自带脆响：kr-i-sp。

normal.en: crispy = crisp + y, the food adjective.
normal.cn: crispy ＝ crisp + y，形容食物的常用变体。

normal.en: Crisp air means dry cool air, not sticky heat.
normal.cn: crisp air 指干爽凉气，不是闷热。

normal.en: A crisp reply answers with no extra words.
normal.cn: crisp reply 回答干脆，没有废话。

normal.en: In Britain, crisps are what Americans call chips.
normal.cn: 在英国 crisps 指薯片，即美式 chips。

abstract.en: Bite an apple and hear the tiny snap ring in your ears.
abstract.cn: 咬一口苹果，听那声脆响在耳边回荡。

abstract.en: Step outside on a January morning and feel the air pinch your cheeks.
abstract.cn: 在冬日清晨出门，感受空气轻掐脸颊的清冽。

abstract.en: See a new banknote folded flat, not one soft corner.
abstract.cn: 看一张挺括的新钞平整折好，没有一个软角。

examples.en: Grandma's biscuits come out of the oven golden and crisp.
examples.cn: 奶奶的饼干出炉时金黄酥脆。

examples.en: The morning air was crisp after last night's rain.
examples.cn: 夜雨过后，清晨的空气格外清爽。

examples.en: Our team captain gave a crisp speech before the game.
examples.cn: 队长赛前作了简短利落的发言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「脆斯铺」——脆响一声「斯」地铺满口腔

root: 来自拉丁语 crispus（卷曲硬挺的），经古法语 cresp 进入英语；词义由「卷曲」演变为「干燥挺硬、一折即断」，故有脆、清爽、利落等义项。

sensesIntro.en: From a snapping bite to cool air to clipped words.
sensesIntro.cn: 从咬下的一声脆响，到清冽的空气，再到简短的话语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean dry snap
core.cn: 核心意象：干脆的断裂声

branches.en: Apples, lettuce and toast
branches.cn: 苹果、生菜和吐司

branches.en: Autumn mornings full of fresh air
branches.cn: 满是清新空气的秋晨

branches.en: Short answers without extra words
branches.cn: 没有废话的简短回答

branches.en: Food turning firm in the pan
branches.cn: 在锅里变脆的食物

branches.en: One snap, two senses
branches.cn: 一声脆响，两种感受

intro.en: Crisp keeps a short Latin root and adds plain English endings.
intro.cn: crisp 保留简短的拉丁词根，加上朴素的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root crispus meant curly and stiff.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 crispus 意为卷曲而硬挺。

definition_zh: 给；给予；赠送；提供；引起；让步（作名词）
definition_en: to hand something to someone, offer it, cause a feeling, or bend slightly under pressure
core_image: 摊开的手掌把东西交到另一只手里
scene: 雨天放学，同桌把伞柄塞进你的手里。 The classmate gave his umbrella to his friend at the school gate.
sceneCN: 这里 give 是「把某物交到对方手里」（第 1 个义项：交付；给予）；句意为同桌在校门口把伞给了朋友。

derivatives.zh: 由 give 加 -er 构成，义为「给予者」
give 的同根名词形式，义为「礼物」
由 give 加 -ing 构成，义为「给予；施予」

senses.title: To hand something over
senses.definition: to put something into someone's hands or offer it to them
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到对方手里或递给对方
senses.example: The classmate gave his umbrella to his friend at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 同桌在校门口把伞给了朋友。
senses.why: The core image is an open hand passing an object forward, the plainest act of transfer.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是摊开的手把物件向前递出，是最直白的转移动作。

senses.title: To cause a feeling or state
senses.definition: to cause someone to have a feeling, problem, or chance
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生某种感觉、问题或机会
senses.example: The long climb gave him a dizzy feeling.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间的攀登使他感到眩晕。
senses.why: What is handed over need not be a thing: a feeling or chance can be placed in someone too.
senses.whyCN: 被递出的不必是实物：感觉与机会同样可以被放到对方身上。

senses.title: To perform or provide
senses.definition: to perform an action such as a speech, or provide help or information
senses.definitionCN: 发表演讲等行为，或提供帮助、信息
senses.example: The head teacher gave a speech at the opening ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在开学典礼上发表了演讲。
senses.why: A speech or help is not an object, yet it passes from speaker to audience like a gift.
senses.whyCN: 演讲与帮助虽非实物，却像礼物一样从一方传到另一方。

senses.title: To bend under pressure
senses.definition: to move or bend slightly when pressed, or to stop resisting
senses.definitionCN: 受压时轻微移动弯曲，或停止抵抗
senses.example: The wooden bridge gives a little when trucks cross.
senses.exampleCN: 木桥在卡车驶过时会轻微下弯。
senses.why: A hand that holds firmly can still loosen a little; materials yield the same way.
senses.whyCN: 握紧的手也会稍微松开；材料同样如此退让。

senses.title: To stop holding or doing
senses.definition: to stop trying or to surrender something, in give up
senses.definitionCN: 在 give up 中表示停止尝试或交出
senses.example: She gave up sugary drinks for a whole year.
senses.exampleCN: 她整整一年没喝含糖饮料。
senses.why: The hand that was holding something opens and lets go, ending the holding.
senses.whyCN: 握着的手摊开松开，持有就此结束。

intro.en: Give is a core Germanic verb, and its noun gift was born from it.
intro.cn: give 是日耳曼语的核心动词，名词 gift 就诞生于它。

items.en: The reconstructed root gebhan meant to give, shared across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 gebhan 意为给予，遍布日耳曼各语言。

items.en: Old Norse gefa shaped the northern form of the verb in England.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 gefa 塑造了英格兰北部该动词的形式。

items.en: Old English giefan meant to give; past tense geaf, participle giefen.
items.cn: 古英语 giefan 意为给予，过去式 geaf，分词 giefen。

items.en: Middle English evened the forms into geven with the modern vowel.
items.cn: 中古英语把词形整化为 geven，元音趋于现代。

items.en: Modern English fixed give, gave, given and extended senses to yielding and causing.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 give、gave、given，并延伸出让步与引起义。

note.en: The words below echo give in sound or live in the same field of handing things over.
note.cn: 以下词与 give 音近，或同属「交付、给予」义场。

entries.definition: To be alive or reside; only the first sound differs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「居住；活着」，与 give 仅首音不同。

entries.definition: The person who gives something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「给予者」，由 give 直接派生。

entries.definition: To stop being angry at a fault; built on give.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「原谅」，由 for- 加 give 构成，同根。

entries.definition: To present something for someone to accept or refuse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提出；提供」，强调对方的接受与否尚待决定。

entries.definition: To give money or goods to a good cause.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「捐赠」，多用于公益语境。

entries.definition: To give something formally, as a right or request.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「准予；授予」，偏正式。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of give.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Give, gave, given is one of English's oldest irregular patterns.
normal.cn: give、gave、given 是英语最古老的不规则变化之一。

normal.en: Forgive and forgive-and-forget keep give inside an older verb family.
normal.cn: forgive 等词让 give 保留在古老的动词家族里。

normal.en: Give in means the hand loosens and resistance ends.
normal.cn: give in 指手松开、抵抗结束。

normal.en: Give off is used for heat, light and smells leaving an object.
normal.cn: give off 用于热量、光和气味从物体散发。

normal.en: The noun give describes how much a seat or rope bends.
normal.cn: 名词 give 描述座椅或绳索的弹性程度。

abstract.en: Picture an open palm tilting forward until the object slides into another hand.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的掌心向前倾，物件滑入另一只手。

abstract.en: See an umbrella handle pushed gently into your grip in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨天里伞柄被轻轻推入你的手中。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge plank sinking a finger's width under a truck, then rising back.
abstract.cn: 想象桥板在卡车下被压低一指宽，随后又回弹。

senses.title: Painful feeling
senses.definition: a painful feeling caused by knowing you did wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因知道自己做错而感到的痛苦
senses.example: He felt shame for lying.
senses.exampleCN: 他因说谎而感到羞愧。
senses.why: This is the central emotional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的情感义项。

senses.title: Disgrace
senses.definition: loss of honour or respect
senses.definitionCN: 荣誉或尊重的丧失
senses.example: The scandal brought shame on the family.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻使这个家庭蒙羞。
senses.why: Shame can be a public state, not only a private feeling.
senses.whyCN: 羞耻可以是公开的状态，而不只是私人感受。

senses.title: To make ashamed
senses.definition: to make someone feel shame
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到羞愧
senses.example: She was shamed by his words.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话让她感到羞愧。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of causing the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为引起这种感觉的动词。

senses.title: A pity
senses.definition: something unfortunate, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 不幸的事，用于口语
senses.example: It is a shame you cannot come.

senses.why: A mild regret is softened by the word shame.
senses.whyCN: 轻微的遗憾用 shame 来缓和。

intro.en: Shame comes from Old English sceamu, a Germanic word for the feeling of disgrace.
intro.cn: shame 源自古英语 sceamu，是日耳曼语中表示羞耻感的词。

items.en: The root named a sense of disgrace.

items.cn: sceamu 意为羞耻或谦逊。

items.cn: 短语 a shame 开始表示可惜。

note.en: Shame is compared with similar-looking words and with words for disgrace.

normalIntro.en: Shame is the heat of being seen doing wrong, and the social mark it leaves.
normalIntro.cn: shame 是被看见做错事时的灼热感，以及它留下的社会印记。

normal.en: He hung his head in shame.
normal.cn: 他羞愧地低下头。

normal.en: The lie brought shame on him.
normal.cn: 谎言让他蒙羞。

normal.en: It is a shame she left early.

normal.en: Shame can stop people from repeating mistakes.
normal.cn: 羞耻能阻止人们重犯错误。

normal.en: He was shamed into apologising.

abstract.en: Shame is a mirror held by other people.
abstract.cn: 羞耻是别人举起的镜子。

abstract.en: Too much shame can teach the wrong lesson.

abstract.en: A pity and a disgrace share one small word.
abstract.cn: 可惜与耻辱共用一个不起眼的词。

definition_zh: 自由的；空闲的；免费的；不受……影响的；释放；使自由
definition_en: not controlled, held, or paid for; having time available; to release someone or something
core_image: 敞开的笼门：锁住了的东西被放出去
scene: 公园免费开放日，孩子们不用买票就跑了进去。 Entry to the park is free on Mondays.
sceneCN: 这里 free 是「免费的」的意思（第 3 个义项：不需要付钱）；周一进公园不用花钱。

derivatives.zh: free 加 -dom 名词后缀，义为「自由；自主」
free 加 -ly，义为「自由地；随意地」
free 加 -er，义为「释放者」
free 复合 man，义为「自由民；有公民权者」

senses.title: Not held or controlled
senses.definition: not held, tied, or controlled by anyone
senses.definitionCN: 没有被束缚或被他人支配的状态。
senses.example: The birds are free to fly where they like.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟儿可以自由地飞往任何地方。
senses.why: The Germanic root frijaz meant beloved, and being among your loved ones meant not being bound.
senses.whyCN: 日耳曼词根 frijaz 意为「亲爱的」，置身所爱之人中间便意味着不被束缚。

senses.title: Having free time
senses.definition: not busy; available to do something
senses.definitionCN: 没有安排、可以用于别处的时间。
senses.example: Are you free this Saturday afternoon?
senses.exampleCN: 你这周六下午有空吗？
senses.why: Not being tied by duties leaves time unbound.
senses.whyCN: 不被事务捆绑，时间便是「未被占用」的。

senses.title: Costing no money
senses.definition: available without payment
senses.definitionCN: 不需要付钱就能获得。
senses.example: Water is free at the school canteen.
senses.exampleCN: 学校食堂的水是免费的。
senses.why: Free of ties becomes free of payment: nothing holds your money.
senses.whyCN: 「不被束缚」延伸到金钱：你的钱没有被「拴走」。

senses.title: Not affected by something bad
senses.definition: not containing or affected by something unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 没有不需要的东西、不受其影响的。
senses.example: The room is free of smoke after the window was opened.
senses.exampleCN: 开窗后房间里没有烟味了。
senses.why: Freedom from something means it cannot reach you.
senses.whyCN: free from 某物，即该物够不到你。

senses.title: To release from holding
senses.definition: to let a person or animal go from a cage, trap, or hold
senses.definitionCN: 把人或动物从笼子、陷阱、控制中放开。
senses.example: Firemen freed the cat from the tall tree.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员把猫从高树上救了下来。
senses.why: The state of being free becomes the act of freeing.
senses.whyCN: 「自由的状态」转为「给自由」的动作。

intro.en: Free carries a warm old meaning: beloved membership, not chains.
intro.cn: free 携带着温暖的古义：「被爱者」的身份，而非「没有锁链」的字面。

items.en: The reconstructed root *frijaz meant beloved, related to friend.
items.cn: 重构词根 *frijaz 意为「亲爱的」，与 friend 同源。

items.en: In early tribes, household members were the free, unenslaved ones.
items.cn: 早期部族中，家庭成员即是「自由人」，区别于奴隶。

items.en: Fre meant free, contrasting with theow (slave).
items.cn: 古英语 fre 意为自由，与 theow（奴隶）相对。

items.en: The senses of free time, no cost, and release all spread.
items.cn: 空闲、免费、释放诸义扩散开来。

items.en: Freedom, freely, and compounds like free of charge became fixed.
items.cn: freedom、freely 及 free of charge 等搭配定型。

note.en: Words shaped like free and words of liberty and release.
note.cn: 与 free 形近的词以及表示自由、释放的词。

abstract.cn: 想象笼门敞开的那一刻。

abstract.en: Picture an empty afternoon with no plans.

examples.cn: 博物馆对学生免费开放。

examples.en: The zoo keepers freed the trapped monkey safely.
examples.cn: 动物园饲养员安全地救出了被困的猴子。

examples.en: I am free after four o'clock if you want to play chess.
examples.cn: 四点以后我有空，如果你想下棋的话。

sensesIntro.en: Free spreads from not being held to spare time, no cost, immunity, and the act of releasing.
sensesIntro.cn: free 从「不被束缚」铺开：空闲时间、零费用、免受影响，最后变成「释放」的动作。

definition_zh: 时期；阶段；周期；课时；句号；经期
definition_en: a length of time, a stage in history or a process, a recurring cycle, a lesson, or the full stop at the end of a sentence
core_image: 一条走了一圈又回到原点的轨道：起点与终点重合，中间那段就是一圈。
scene: 维多利亚时代，世界上第一批地下铁路开始运行。 The Victorian period saw the first underground railways in the world.
sceneCN: 这里 period 是「历史上的一段时期」（第 2 个义项：时代、阶段）；句意：维多利亚时期出现了世界上最早的地下铁路。场景要点：煤气灯、砖砌车站、旧式火车；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A length of time with limits
senses.definition: a length of time during which something happens, especially one with a clear beginning and end
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生所经历的一段时间，尤指有明确起止的
senses.example: The study covered a period of five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究覆盖了五年时间。
senses.why: Greek periodos was 'a going around', from peri 'around' + hodos 'way'. A measured stretch of time is a closed loop with a start and a finish.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 periodos 是“绕行一周”，由 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路”构成。被量出的一段时光，就是一个有起点和终点的闭环。

senses.title: A stage of history
senses.definition: a particular stretch of history with its own character, style, or events
senses.definitionCN: 具有自身特征、风格或事件的历史阶段
senses.example: The country changed its alphabet twice in that period.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在那个时期两次更换文字。
senses.why: History is cut into loops: a culture goes through a way of doing things and comes out the other side, leaving a named stretch behind.
senses.whyCN: 历史被切成一圈一圈：一种文化走完一套做法，从另一边出来，留下一段被命名的时光。

senses.title: A recurring cycle
senses.definition: a regular interval after which an event or process repeats
senses.definitionCN: 某一事件或过程重复出现所间隔的固定时间
senses.example: The comet returns every 76 years, its orbital period.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗彗星每 76 年回归一次，这就是它的轨道周期。
senses.why: This is the most literal sense: a body goes around and comes back to the same place. The interval is the time the loop takes.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的义项：一个物体绕行一圈，回到同一位置。这个间隔就是那一圈所花的时间。

senses.title: One lesson in a school day
senses.definition: one of the fixed blocks of time into which a school day is divided
senses.definitionCN: 学校一天被划分成的若干个固定时间段之一
senses.example: We have two periods of chemistry on Tuesdays.
senses.exampleCN: 我们周二有两节化学课。
senses.why: The school day is cut into loops of equal length. Each block is a period because it is a closed, measured unit that ends when the bell rings.
senses.whyCN: 学校的一天被切成等长的圈。每一格都是 period，因为它是一个封闭的、被量出的单位，铃响就结束。

senses.title: The full stop in punctuation
senses.definition: the mark at the end of a declarative sentence
senses.definitionCN: 陈述句末尾的那个标点
senses.example: Delete the extra period at the end of the citation.
senses.exampleCN: 删掉引文末尾多余的那个句号。
senses.why: Recorded from the 1580s. A sentence is a loop of thought; the full stop closes the loop, which is why the mark took the name of a completed cycle.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 80 年代见于记录。一个句子是一圈思想；句号把这一圈合上，所以这个符号借用了“完成一个周期”的名字。

senses.title: Menstruation
senses.titleCN: 经期：按月转回的那几天
senses.definition: the monthly bleeding cycle in a person who menstruates, or the time it lasts
senses.definitionCN: 有月经的人每月一次的出血周期，或该周期持续的几天
senses.example: The app tracks the length of each period.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用记录每次经期的长度。
senses.why: Recorded from 1822. The bodily cycle returns at a regular interval, so the medical use simply names the most visible human example of a period.
senses.whyCN: 1822 年见于记录。身体周期按固定间隔转回来，医学用法只是把人类最可见的一个“周期”例子叫成了 period。

senses.title: One division of a sports game
senses.titleCN: 比赛分节：把一场球切成几段
senses.definition: one of the equal parts into which a game such as ice hockey is divided
senses.definitionCN: 冰球等比赛中把整场划分成的若干个等长时间段之一
senses.example: They scored twice in the second period.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在第二节里进了两球。
senses.why: A game is another closed stretch of time divided into loops. Each period starts with a face-off and ends with a whistle.
senses.whyCN: 一场比赛也是一段被切成若干圈的封闭时间。每一节从开球开始，到哨响结束。

senses.title: Belonging to a past style
senses.titleCN: 仿古的：带着某个时代的样子
senses.definition: of furniture, costume, or a work, made in or imitating the style of a particular historical period
senses.definitionCN: 指家具、服装或作品按某一历史时期的风格制作或仿制
senses.example: The room was furnished with period pieces from the 1780s.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里摆着 1780 年代的仿古家具。
senses.why: The noun becomes an adjective: an object carries the look of a named loop of history, so it is 'period' rather than merely old.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为形容词：一件物品带着某段被命名的历史圈的样子，所以它是“时期的”，而不只是“旧的”。

intro.en: Period is Greek periodos 'a going around', from peri 'around' + hodos 'way'. English borrowed it through Latin and first used it for a cycle of time.
intro.cn: period 是希腊语 periodos“绕行一周”，由 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路”构成。英语经拉丁语借入，最早用来指时间的循环。

items.en: Hodos meant 'way, road, journey'. It survives in English compounds such as method ('a way along') and period.
items.cn: hodos 意为“路、道路、行程”。它保留在英语的 method（“沿路而行”）与 period 等复合词里。

items.en: Periodos meant 'a going around, a circuit, a cycle', used of the sun's course and of rhetorical sentences that round off.
items.cn: periodos 意为“绕行、一圈、循环”，用于太阳的运行，也用于首尾完整、能收口的修辞句子。

items.en: Latin took periodus as a term of astronomy and rhetoric. Its sense of a rounded sentence is why the closing mark later took this name.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 periodus 作为天文学与修辞学术语使用。它“首尾完整的句子”这一义，正是后来收尾标点取这个名字的原因。

items.en: English records period around 1400 meaning 'course, extent of time, cycle'. The historical sense 'a named age' develops from this.
items.cn: 英语在 1400 年前后记录 period，意为“进程、时间长度、周期”。历史的“被命名的时代”义由此发展而来。

items.en: The punctuation sense is recorded in the 1580s. A full stop is literally the mark that closes the period of a sentence.
items.cn: 标点义于 16 世纪 80 年代见于记录。句号字面上就是“合上一句话的那一圈”的记号。

items.en: The menstrual sense is recorded from 1822, and the school and sports senses follow the same model: a day or a game cut into closed blocks of time.
items.cn: 经期义于 1822 年见于记录；课时与比赛分节义遵循同样的模式：把一天或一场比赛切成封闭的时间块。

note.en: The first group is the period family plus compounds built on it; the second collects words for stretches of time.
note.cn: 第一组是 period 词族及由它构成的复合词；第二组收“时间段”类近义词。

entries.definition: happening at regular intervals, or relating to a period. It is the adjective of period, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔发生的；与周期有关的。它是 period 的形容词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: a magazine published at regular intervals, or published regularly. The noun sense is a publication, not a time span.
entries.definitionCN: 定期出版的杂志；定期出版的。名词指出版物，不是时间段。

entries.definition: an object or work valued for its style from a past era. Here period works as an adjective meaning 'of a historical era'.
entries.definitionCN: 因带有过去时代风格而有价值的物品或作品。这里 period 作形容词，意为“某一历史时代的”。

entries.definition: the quality of occurring in regular cycles. It names the abstract property behind periodic.
entries.definitionCN: 按规律周期发生的性质。它命名 periodic 背后的抽象属性。

entries.definition: a long period of history named after a system, leader, or event. It is usually larger and more formal than period.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种制度、领袖或事件命名的长历史阶段。它通常比 period 更大、更正式。

entries.definition: a period that begins with a striking change and is treated as a new starting point. It stresses the break, not just the length.
entries.definitionCN: 以显著变化开始、被视为新起点的时期。它强调断裂，而不只是长度。

entries.definition: a long stretch of history associated with a way of life, as in the Bronze Age or the age of the internet. It is looser than period.
entries.definitionCN: 与某种生活方式相关联的长历史阶段，如青铜时代、互联网时代。它比 period 宽松。

entries.definition: a fixed length of time for which something lasts, such as a school term or a prison term. It is defined by an agreement or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物持续的固定时长，如学期、刑期。它由约定或规则界定。

entries.definition: a short period of a particular activity or weather. It is informal and almost always short.
entries.definitionCN: 某活动或天气的一小段。它口语化，且几乎总是很短。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Greek peri 'around' + hodos 'way', giving periodos 'a going around'. Family words periodic, periodical, periodically, periodicity, and compounds period piece and grace period.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：希腊语 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路”，合成 periodos“绕行一周”。词族为 periodic、periodical、periodically、periodicity，以及复合词 period piece、grace period。

normal.en: Period and method share hodos 'way': one is a way around, the other a way along.
normal.cn: period 与 method 共享 hodos“路”：一个是绕一圈的路，一个是沿着走的路。

normal.en: A full stop is called a period because it closes the sentence's circuit.
normal.cn: 句号叫 period，是因为它把句子的回路合上。

normal.en: A school day is cut into periods the way a circle is cut into arcs.
normal.cn: 学校的一天被切成 period，就像圆被切成弧。

normal.en: Periodic table: elements arranged by repeating cycles of properties.
normal.cn: 元素周期表：按性质重复的周期排列元素。

normal.en: A period piece is an object still wearing the clothes of its era.
normal.cn: period piece 是一件还穿着它那个时代衣服的物品。

abstract.en: History is only manageable because we agree to cut it into loops.
abstract.cn: 历史之所以可处理，只是因为我们同意把它切成一圈一圈。

abstract.en: A period is a promise that the sentence will end.
abstract.cn: 句号是一个承诺：这句话会结束。

abstract.en: Every cycle is a way of saying that the same place can be reached again.
abstract.cn: 每一个周期，都是在说同一个地方还能再被抵达。

examples.en: Sales rose sharply over the same period last year.
examples.cn: 销售额在去年同期那段时期大幅上升。

examples.en: The teacher gave us ten minutes at the end of the period.
examples.cn: 老师在那一节课末尾给了我们十分钟。

examples.en: Put a period at the end of every complete sentence.
examples.cn: 每个完整的句子末尾都要加句号。

dict_mnemonic.text: “皮瑞尔的”——皮瑞尔的怀表每绕一圈就响一次，一圈就是一段 → period 周期、时期

root: 源自希腊语 periodos“绕行一周”，由 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路、行程”构成；经拉丁语 periodus、古法语进入英语，约 1400 年义为“进程、时长、周期”。核心是“绕一圈所花的那段时间”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of period, all one shape: a closed stretch that begins, runs its course, and comes back to an end.
sensesIntro.cn: period 的八个义项是同一个形状：一段封闭的时间，开始、走完、回到终点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a track that leaves a point, goes all the way around, and returns to the same point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从某点出发、绕行一圈、又回到同一点的轨道。

branches.en: SPAN: from a five-year study to the Victorian age, every span is a loop someone has marked off.
branches.cn: 跨度：从五年的研究到维多利亚时代，每一段都是有人划出的一圈。

branches.en: REPETITION: an orbit and a hockey game both return to the start on a schedule.
branches.cn: 重复：轨道与冰球比赛，都按时刻表回到起点。

branches.en: BODY AND SCHOOL: the timetable and the monthly cycle are the same closed block imposed on living time.
branches.cn: 身体与学校：课表与月度周期，都是加在活的时间上的同一种封闭块。

branches.en: PUNCTUATION: the mark that closes a sentence borrows the name of a completed circuit.
branches.cn: 标点：合上句子的符号，借用了“完成一圈”的名字。

branches.en: STYLE: an object can still carry the look of the loop it was made in.
branches.cn: 风格：一件物品仍然带着它被造出时那一圈的样子。

intro.en: Period's family is built on the Greek compound periodos. Suffixes turn it into an adjective, an adverb, and a noun of property; compounds name the things people measure in cycles.
intro.cn: period 的词族建立在希腊复合词 periodos 上。后缀把它变成形容词、副词与属性名词；复合词则命名人们按周期计量的东西。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are Greek hodos 'way', periodos 'circuit', and Latin periodus, the borrowing English received. Latin added no new root.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是希腊语 hodos“路”、periodos“一圈”与拉丁语借形 periodus，英语承接的正是后者。拉丁语没有新增词根。

items.meaning: occurring at regular intervals; relating to a period
items.meaningCN: 按固定间隔发生的；与周期有关的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The system runs a periodic backup every night.
items.exampleCN: 系统每晚执行一次定期备份。

items.meaning: published at regular intervals; a magazine so published
items.meaningCN: 定期出版的；定期刊物（-al 构成形容词，也可作名词）
items.example: The library keeps back issues of the periodical.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆保存这份期刊的过刊。

items.meaningCN: 定期地；周期性地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: the quality of recurring in cycles
items.meaningCN: 按周期重复的性质（-ity 构成属性名词）
items.example: The periodicity of the signal suggests a rotating source.
items.exampleCN: 信号的周期性表明源头在旋转。

items.meaning: a work or object valued for its historical style
items.meaningCN: 因历史风格而有价值的作品或物品
items.example: The film is a period piece set in 1912.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影是设定在 1912 年的年代戏。

items.meaning: extra time allowed before a penalty applies
items.meaningCN: 在处罚生效前额外允许的时间
items.example: The bank offers a ten-day grace period.

items.meaning: a particular stretch of time being discussed
items.meaningCN: 正在讨论的某一特定时间段
items.example: Over this time period, prices doubled.
items.exampleCN: 在这段时间里，价格上涨了一倍。

items.example: She takes two days off for period pain each month.
items.exampleCN: 她每月因经期疼痛休息两天。

items.meaning: the arrangement of elements by repeating chemical properties
items.meaningCN: 按化学性质重复规律排列元素的表格
items.example: Carbon sits in the second row of the periodic table.
items.exampleCN: 碳位于元素周期表第二行。

items.meaning: clothing made in the style of a historical era
items.meaningCN: 按历史时期风格制作的服装
items.example: The actors wore period costume in every scene.
items.exampleCN: 演员在每一场都穿年代服装。

latinEntries.meaning: a circuit; a complete sentence; a cycle of time
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一圈；完整的句子；时间周期

definition_zh: 有病的；不健康的；坏的；恶劣的；有害地
definition_en: not healthy, bad or harmful, or badly
core_image: 脸色发白地躺着；事情往坏里走
scene: 教室里有张座位空着。 He stayed home because he felt ill.
sceneCN: 这里 ill 是「有病的」（第 1 个义项：身体不舒服）；句意：他因为感觉生病而待在家里。

pos.zh: 恶行；不幸；the ills：种种弊病

derivatives.zh: 疾病；ill 加名词后缀
不识字的；同前缀构词
非法的；同前缀异源词

senses.title: Sick and unwell
senses.definition: suffering from sickness or poor health
senses.definitionCN: 遭受疾病或健康不佳
senses.example: The baby fell ill during the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在旅途中病倒了。
senses.why: The word paints a body gone pale and weak.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描绘一副苍白虚弱的身体。

senses.title: Bad or unfavorable
senses.definition: bad in quality or bringing harm
senses.definitionCN: 质量差或带来损害
senses.example: The plan met with ill luck from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这计划从一开始就运气不佳。
senses.why: Sickness is a bad state, so the word widens to anything bad.
senses.whyCN: 生病是坏状态，词义便扩展到一切坏事。

senses.title: Hostile or unfriendly
senses.definition: showing hostility or bad intent
senses.definitionCN: 表现出敌意或坏心思
senses.example: He bore no ill feeling toward the judge.
senses.exampleCN: 他对法官并无恶意。
senses.why: A bad heart is the illness of feelings.
senses.whyCN: 坏心肠是情感的病。

senses.title: Badly, in an adverbial way
senses.definition: badly or poorly, in set phrases
senses.definitionCN: 在固定短语中表示差、糟
senses.example: The proposal was ill received.
senses.exampleCN: 该提案反响恶劣。
senses.why: The adjective bends into the adverb: done in a bad way.
senses.whyCN: 形容词弯成副词：以糟糕的方式做成。

senses.title: Social problems as ills
senses.definition: problems or evils in society
senses.definitionCN: 社会中的问题或弊病
senses.example: Poverty and crime are the ills of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 贫困与犯罪是这座城市的弊病。
senses.why: Bad states collected together become named evils.
senses.whyCN: 各种坏状态集合起来，就成了有名目的恶。

intro.en: Ill comes from Old Norse illr, bad, borrowed into northern Middle English where it pushed aside the older sick in many uses. The Norse source itself is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: ill 来自古诺斯语 illr「坏」，借入北部中古英语，在许多用法中排挤了旧词 sick；诺斯语源头本身来源不确定。

items.en: Old Norse illr meant bad, evil or hard; its ultimate root is uncertain.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 illr 意为坏的、恶的、艰难的；其更早词根不确定。

items.en: Middle English ill entered through the north and first meant bad in a general way.
items.cn: 中古英语 ill 经北方进入，最初泛指坏。

items.en: By the fifteenth century ill was common for sickness, especially in northern usage.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，ill 已常用于疾病，尤见于北方用法。

items.en: Modern English split the register: ill for serious sickness and set phrases, sick for everyday vomiting and American illness.
items.cn: 现代英语分化语域：ill 指重病与固定短语，sick 指日常病态与美式用法。

items.en: The adverbial and noun uses solidified in phrases like ill advised and the ills of society.
items.cn: 副词与名词用法在 ill advised、the ills of society 等短语中固化。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the ill family and close spellings. The meaning group compares sickness and badness words.
note.cn: 形近组区分 ill 词族与相近拼写；词义组比较疾病与恶劣用词。

entries.definition: the state of being ill; a disease.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病。本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: illegal or forbidden. Starts the same but comes from Latin licere, to be allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 非法的。开头相同，但源自拉丁语 licere「被允许」。

entries.definition: a raised area of land; one letter changes everything.
entries.definitionCN: 小山。一个字母之差，意义全变。

entries.definition: unwell; in American English the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 生病的。美式英语的日常用词。

entries.definition: in poor health, in a gentle polite way.
entries.definitionCN: 欠安。委婉礼貌的说法。

entries.definition: often ill and weak-looking.
entries.definitionCN: 多病的。常病且显得虚弱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the fall ill phrase, the worse-worst comparison and the ill will collocation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用 fall ill 短语、worse-worst 比较级链和 ill will 搭配。

normal.en: fall ill is the standard way to become sick in formal English.
normal.cn: fall ill 是正式英语里「生病」的标准说法。

normal.en: ill has no own comparatives: ill, worse, worst.
normal.cn: ill 没有自己的比较级：ill、worse、worst。

normal.en: ill will is a bad heart made into a phrase.
normal.cn: ill will 把坏心肠固定成短语。

normal.en: speak ill of means to badmouth; the adverb hides in it.
normal.cn: speak ill of 指说坏话；副词藏在其中。

normal.en: ill-fated joins ill to fate: a doomed journey from the start.
normal.cn: ill-fated 把 ill 接到 fate 上：从一开始就注定失败。

abstract.en: One image: a pale face and a turned-down mouth.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：苍白的脸和向下撇的嘴。

abstract.en: Ill travels from body to luck to heart to society.
abstract.cn: ill 从身体游走到运气、人心乃至社会。

abstract.en: Register matters: doctors write ill, friends say sick.
abstract.cn: 语域很重要：医生写 ill，朋友说 sick。

examples.en: She has been ill for two weeks.
examples.cn: 她病了两周了。

examples.en: The bridge was an ill-designed structure.
examples.cn: 这座桥是个设计恶劣的结构。

examples.en: No ill feeling remained after the talk.
examples.cn: 会谈之后再无恶意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一偶」：一偶感风寒，人就 ill 了。

root: 古诺斯语 illr「坏」（来源不确定），经北部中古英语借入；词义路径为「坏→有病的→恶意的→副词恶劣地→名词社会弊病」；比较级用 worse、worst。

sensesIntro.en: Ill starts as plain badness, settles on sickness, turns hostile, bends into an adverb, and collects into the noun ills for society's evils.
sensesIntro.cn: ill 从单纯的坏出发，落定于疾病，转向敌意，弯成副词，最后聚合成指社会之恶的名词 ills。

core.en: Something gone wrong: in a body, a plan, a heart or a city.
core.cn: 出了岔子的东西：身体、计划、内心或城市。

branches.en: HEALTH: ill health, fall ill.
branches.cn: 健康：ill health、fall ill。

branches.en: QUALITY: ill luck, ill-fated.
branches.cn: 品质：ill luck、ill-fated。

branches.en: HEART: ill will, ill feeling.
branches.cn: 人心：ill will、ill feeling。

branches.en: MANNER: ill received, ill advised.
branches.cn: 方式：ill received、ill advised。

branches.en: SOCIETY: the ills of poverty and crime.
branches.cn: 社会：贫困与犯罪之弊。

intro.en: Ill compounds freely: illness, ill-fated, illiterate-lookalikes and the classic ill will.
intro.cn: ill 构词自由：illness、ill-fated、形近的 illiterate 系，以及经典的 ill will。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty: ill is a Norse loan, unrelated to Latin malus or the prefix in-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空：ill 是诺斯语借词，与拉丁语 malus 及前缀 in- 无关。

items.example: The crew fell ill on the voyage.
Illness kept him out of school.
The book lists the ills of modern work.
items.exampleCN: 这本书列举现代职场的弊病。

items.example: The ill-fated expedition lost its ships.
items.exampleCN: 这次厄运缠身的远征失去了船只。

definition_zh: 菜单；菜谱；（电脑）菜单；选项列表
definition_en: a list of dishes served in a restaurant, or a list of choices shown on a screen or offered by a service
core_image: 一张折起的纸，上面一行行写着今天能点的菜
scene: 餐馆门口的木架上夹着一张纸，客人进门先低头看它。 At the counter, the waiter handed us a menu with today's specials.
sceneCN: 这里是「菜单」（第 1 个义项：餐馆里列出菜品的单子）；句意为在柜台边，服务员递给我们一张写着当日特色菜的菜单。图中可辨识物件：木架、夹子、折起的纸单。

pos.zh: 菜单；菜谱；（电脑）菜单；选项列表

derivatives.zh: 由 sub-（下、次级）加 menu 构成，义为「子菜单」
由 menu 与 driven 复合而成，义为「菜单驱动的」
由 menu 与 bar 复合而成，义为「菜单栏」

senses.title: A list of dishes in a restaurant
senses.definition: a list of the food that a restaurant can serve, often with prices
senses.definitionCN: 餐馆可供应的食物清单，通常附价格
senses.example: The menu changes with the season.
senses.exampleCN: 菜单随季节更换。
senses.why: The French word first meant a small, detailed list; a restaurant's bill of fare is exactly such a detailed list, so the label stuck to food.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语词最初指「细小而详细的清单」；餐馆的菜品单正是一份这样的详细清单，于是这个称呼就落到了食物上。

senses.title: A list of choices on a computer screen
senses.definition: a list of commands or choices that appears on a screen and can be selected
senses.definitionCN: 出现在屏幕上、可供选择的命令或选项列表
senses.example: Open the file menu and choose save.
senses.exampleCN: 打开文件菜单，选择保存。
senses.why: A screen menu is a list of what you may pick, which is the same shape as a bill of fare: many items, one choice.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕菜单是一份「你可以挑什么」的清单，形状和菜品单一样：很多项目，只选一个。

senses.title: A range of services or options offered
senses.definition: the set of services or possibilities that an organization makes available
senses.definitionCN: 某个机构所能提供的一整套服务或可能性
senses.example: The clinic offers a wide menu of treatments.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所提供种类繁多的治疗方案。
senses.why: Once menu means a list to choose from, it can leave the restaurant and describe any organized set of options, such as treatments or courses.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 menu 表示「供人挑选的清单」，它就能离开餐馆，去描述任何被整理好的选项集合，例如治疗方案或课程。

intro.en: Menu is a French word for something small and detailed; the restaurant sense grew out of the idea of a finely itemized list.
intro.cn: menu 是法语中表示「细小而详细」的词；餐馆义正是从「分得很细的清单」这个想法长出来的。

items.en: Minutus, the past participle of minuere, meant made small or minute, and it is the source of the French adjective.
items.cn: minutus 是 minuere 的过去分词，意为「被弄小的、微小的」，是法语形容词的来源。

items.en: Minuere meant to lessen or make smaller, and its root min- still marks words about smallness.
items.cn: minuere 意为「减少、使变小」，它的词根 min- 至今标记着与「小」有关的词。

items.en: French menu was an adjective meaning small, fine or detailed, and a menu could be a detailed list written in small writing.
items.cn: 法语 menu 是形容词，意为「小的、精细的、详细的」，而一份 menu 可以是用小字写成的详细清单。

items.en: English borrowed menu in the eighteenth century for a bill of fare, at first as a somewhat fashionable French term.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 menu 指菜品单，起初还带点法语时髦词的意味。

items.en: Modern English extended the word to lists of commands on a screen and, by analogy, to any organized set of choices.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到屏幕上的命令列表，并类推到任何整理好的选择集合。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin root for small or merely similar in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers other words for a list of choices.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「小」词根上、或只是拼写相像的词；近义组收其他表示「选择清单」的词。

entries.definition: Very small; from Latin minutus, the same root as menu.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；来自拉丁语 minutus，与 menu 同根。

entries.definition: A slow elegant dance; its French name goes back to menu, small, because of its small steps.
entries.definitionCN: 一种缓慢优雅的舞蹈；其法语名称可追溯到 menu（小的），因舞步细碎。

entries.definition: The smallest possible amount; built on Latin minimus, from the same root as minuere.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最小量；建立在拉丁语 minimus 上，与 minuere 同根。

entries.definition: A book of instructions; from Latin manus, hand, so only the spelling resembles menu.
entries.definitionCN: 说明书；来自拉丁语 manus（手），只是拼写与 menu 相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: An old phrase for a menu, listing the dishes and their prices.
entries.definitionCN: menu 的旧说法，列出菜品与价格。

entries.definition: A series of items written or printed one after another.
entries.definitionCN: 一条条写出或印出的项目。

entries.definition: A complete list of things, often arranged in order.
entries.definitionCN: 常按顺序排列的完整清单。

entries.definition: A group of things from which one may choose.
entries.definitionCN: 可供从中挑选的一组东西。

normalIntro.en: The word began as an adjective for small, fine detail and ends as a name for any list you pick from.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从表示「细小、精细」的形容词出发，最后成了任何「供你挑选的清单」的名字。

normal.en: Minutus in Latin means made small, so a menu is literally a list written out in small, fine detail.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 minutus 意为「被弄小的」，所以 menu 字面上就是一份写得细小而详细的清单。

normal.en: The min- root in minimum and minute marks smallness, and menu belongs to that same family.
normal.cn: minimum 与 minute 里的 min- 词根标记「小」，menu 属于同一族。

normal.en: A restaurant menu and a computer menu are both lists of things you may choose, which is why one word serves both.
normal.cn: 餐馆菜单和电脑菜单都是「你可以挑什么」的清单，所以一个词身兼两用。

normal.en: Menu bar and drop-down menu are compounds: the second word tells you where or how the list appears.
normal.cn: menu bar 与 drop-down menu 都是复合词，后一个词说明清单出现在哪里、以何种方式出现。

normal.en: Menu of services shows the word escaping the restaurant: any organized set of options can be a menu.
normal.cn: menu of services 显示这个词已经离开餐馆：任何整理好的选项集合都可以叫 menu。

abstract.en: Think of a folded card by the door: it lists what the house can offer before you even sit down.
abstract.cn: 想象门口一张折起的卡片：你还没坐下，它就把这家店能提供什么列给你看。

abstract.en: A menu is a map of choices, not the meal itself; it promises without feeding you.
abstract.cn: menu 是一张选择的地图，不是饭本身；它作出承诺，却不喂饱你。

abstract.en: The same word on a screen reminds us that a list of options is now the shape of modern work.
abstract.cn: 同一个词出现在屏幕上，提醒我们：选项清单已经成了现代工作的形状。

examples.en: The menu changes with the season.
examples.cn: 菜单随季节更换。

examples.en: Open the file menu and choose save.
examples.cn: 打开文件菜单，选择保存。

examples.en: The clinic offers a wide menu of treatments.
examples.cn: 这家诊所提供种类繁多的治疗方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没牛」——菜单上写着没有牛肉，顾客只好换一道；menu 是菜单。

root: 法语 menu（细小、详细）来自拉丁语 minutus（微小的），词根 min- 表示「小」；同族词多与「小、减少」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a detailed list to choose from; it divides into the restaurant list, the screen list, and any organized set of services.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一份供人挑选的详细清单；它分出餐馆菜品单、屏幕选项单，以及任何整理好的服务方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded card by the door listing, line by line, what can be ordered.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口一张折起的卡片，一行行写着今天能点什么。

branches.en: a folded card clipped to a stand by the door
branches.cn: 夹在门口架子上的折页

branches.en: a line of dishes with prices beside them
branches.cn: 一行行菜品，旁边标着价格

branches.en: a list dropping down from the top of a screen
branches.cn: 从屏幕顶部垂下来的列表

branches.en: a clinic handing out a sheet of treatments
branches.cn: 诊所递出一张写满治疗项目的单子

branches.en: one shape of choosing, two places to choose from
branches.cn: 同一种挑选的形状，出现在两个地方

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin adjective of smallness and its verb, then turned into an English noun that now names any list of choices.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「小」的拉丁形容词及其动词构成，后来变成英语名词，如今指任何选择清单。

latinIntro.en: A Latin adjective of smallness and its verb lead to the French word, which English then took over.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「小」的拉丁形容词及其动词导向法语词形，英语再整体借入。

definition_zh: 深的；深沉的；深厚的；深刻的
definition_en: going far down from the top; very strong or serious
core_image: 从表面一直往下走不到底的距离
scene: 游泳馆里，教练告诉我们浅水区和深水区的分界线。 The pool has a deep end for good swimmers only.
sceneCN: 这里 deep 是「深的」（第 1 个义项：向下延伸很远）；句意是泳池只有游得好的同学才能去深水区。

derivatives.zh: 由 deep 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「深深地」
由 deep 的旧形加名词后缀 -th 构成，义为「深度」
由 deep 加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「加深」

senses.title: Going far down from the top
senses.definition: going or reaching far down from the surface
senses.definitionCN: 从表面向下延伸很远
senses.example: The well is so deep that our voices echo back.
senses.exampleCN: 这口井很深，我们的声音会传回回声。
senses.why: Measuring downward distance gave the word its first picture: far from surface to bottom.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的画面就是向下的距离：从表面到底部很远，便有了「深」。

senses.title: Very strong or serious
senses.definition: very strong, serious or hard to change
senses.definitionCN: 非常强烈、认真或难以改变
senses.example: She has a deep love for old songs.
senses.exampleCN: 她对老歌有深厚的热爱。
senses.why: Feelings buried far inside are hard to reach, so strong emotion borrowed the distance image.
senses.whyCN: 藏在心底很深的感情难以触碰，强烈的情感便借用了「远距」的画面。

senses.title: Hard to understand
senses.definition: difficult to understand or full of meaning
senses.definitionCN: 难以理解或意味深长
senses.example: Grandpa's short sayings are often deep.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷的短句常常意味深长。
senses.why: Meaning hidden below the surface takes effort to dig out.
senses.whyCN: 藏在表面之下的含义需要挖掘，于是「深」也指道理深奥。

intro.en: Deep goes back to Old English words for far down.
intro.cn: deep 可追溯到古英语中表示「往下很远」的词。

items.en: The word deop meant far down, extending far below the surface.
items.cn: 古英语 deop 意为往下的很远、低于表面很多。

items.en: It belongs to a Germanic family of depth words.
items.cn: 它属于日耳曼语族的深度词族。

items.en: The spelling settled as deep, and the noun depth grew from the old form deop with -th.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 deep，名词 depth 由旧形 deop 加 -th 构成。

items.en: Writers used it of feelings and thought, not only of water and holes.
items.cn: 作家开始用它形容感情与思绪，不再只指水和洞穴。

items.en: Modern English keeps all senses: deep water, deep sleep, deep thought.
items.cn: 现代英语保留各义项：deep water、deep sleep、deep thought。

note.en: These words share the deep family or describe far-down distance.
note.cn: 这些词属于 deep 词族，或同样描述向下的距离。

entries.definition: more deep
entries.definitionCN: 更深的

entries.definition: the noun of deep
entries.definitionCN: 深度

entries.definition: to make or become deeper
entries.definitionCN: 加深

entries.definition: to consider, different root
entries.definitionCN: 认为（拼写相近，词源无关）

entries.definition: an animal, different root
entries.definitionCN: 鹿（拼写相近，词源无关）

entries.definition: very deep, formal
entries.definitionCN: 深刻的（较正式）

entries.definition: not deep
entries.definitionCN: 浅的（反义）

entries.definition: strong and serious
entries.definitionCN: 沉重的；强烈的

entries.definition: not light or joking
entries.definitionCN: 认真的；严肃的

entries.definition: having no bottom
entries.definitionCN: 无底的

normalIntro.en: Use the well image and the deep family to remember the word.
normalIntro.cn: 用「深井」的画面和 deep 词族记住这个词。

normal.en: deep describes distance downward.
normal.cn: deep 描述向下的距离。

normal.en: depth is the noun: the depth of a pool.
normal.cn: 名词是 depth：the depth of a pool（泳池深度）。

normal.en: deepen the river means make it deeper.
normal.cn: deepen the river 表示把河道加深。

normal.en: two e in the middle: d-e-e-p.
normal.cn: 中间有两个 e：d-e-e-p。

normal.en: take a deep breath before you speak.
normal.cn: 开口前先 take a deep breath（深呼吸）。

abstract.en: Picture a well with no visible bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一口看不见底的水井。

abstract.en: Feel a friendship that grows year after year.
abstract.cn: 体会一年一年生长的友谊。

abstract.en: Hear a sentence that keeps giving meaning each time you read it.
abstract.cn: 听一句每读一次都有新含义的话。

examples.en: The river near our school is too deep for swimming.
examples.cn: 我们学校附近的河太深，不能下去游泳。

examples.en: I took a deep breath before going on stage.
examples.cn: 上台前我深吸了一口气。

examples.en: This book is deep, so I read it slowly.
examples.cn: 这本书很深奥，所以我读得很慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「地铺」——地铺要睡得香，得「深」度睡眠

root: 来自古英语 deop（往下很远），属日耳曼语族的深度词族；名词 depth 由旧形加名词后缀 -th 构成。

sensesIntro.en: Deep measures downward distance, then dives into feelings and meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: deep 先丈量向下的距离，再潜入感情与含义的深处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: distance from surface to bottom
core.cn: 核心意象：从表面到深处的距离

branches.en: Water, wells and holes
branches.cn: 水、井与洞穴

branches.en: Strong buried feelings
branches.cn: 深藏的强烈感情

branches.en: Meaning below the surface
branches.cn: 表面之下的含义

branches.en: Digging both soil and sense
branches.cn: 既挖土也挖道理

branches.en: What lies far inside
branches.cn: 藏在深处的东西

intro.en: Deep is a short root with a small family of depth words.
intro.cn: deep 是个短词根，带着一小圈深度词族。

latinIntro.en: Deep is Germanic, so it has no Latin relatives here.
latinIntro.cn: deep 属日耳曼语源，这里没有拉丁同族词。
